To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) words that are more common in headlines tend to attract more clicks than less frequent words; (ii) words with high click-values tend to be more frequent and more informative in the news article body; (iii) words in headlines that have higher click-values tend to have higher word frequencies; (iv) words with high word frequencies and higher click-values are more informative than words that are less frequent and less informative.
(1) the click-value of a word in a headline is affected by its topical context and (2) the click-values of words in headlines can be learned from aggregate click-through data.

1) words with high click values are not always popular words; 2) words with high popularity are not always words with high click value; 3) the click-value of a word depends on both topical context and temporal context.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how to leverage the large amount of click-through data to better understand the effect of words in headlines on CTR.
the question of how to compete online for news audience, and we provide a novel method for modeling words that attract clicks.
the problem of how to compete for online audience by crafting effective headlines.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the click-based topic model provides an accurate and practical method to identify words that will attract clicks in the future for news headlines.
our proposed model is able to identify words that are most relevant to the current audience, and thus is useful to both journalists and online news publishers.
the headline click-through rate is a good proxy to measure how well a headline attracts clicks.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
by jointly taking topical context and click-through information into account, we can improve headline generation by up to 20% in terms of CTR.
our proposed HCTM model can help online news outlets to better understand the effect of words in headlines on user click-through rate, and thus help them to better compete for online audience.
we have developed a novel model to analyze and model the effect of words and topics on the CTR of headlines.
The main takeaway from our work is that
by leveraging clicks on previously published news headlines, we can improve the performance of headline generation for future articles.
by modeling the relationship between words in headlines and clicks we can significantly improve the quality of headlines for news articles.
by leveraging large-scale click-through information we can improve the performance of headline generation and retrieval tasks.
